cases.name: by-object-number
cases.covers: The ordinary case: an indirect annotation addressed by its object number. Two replies point at it, so this also shows what a delete does NOT clean up.

cases.name: by-nm
cases.covers: A direct annotation with an /NM, which has no object number at all. Its only address is its name.

cases.name: by-index-onto-a-durable-annotation
cases.covers: An index reference that lands on an annotation with an object number. The reported id is the one it turned out to have, not the one it was asked for.

cases.name: by-index-onto-a-weak-annotation
cases.covers: An index reference onto the annotation with no object number and no /NM. Nothing durable to report, so the result is null and the caller learns it must re-read.

cases.name: by-index-onto-an-empty-nm
cases.covers: The annotation whose /NM is present and empty. An empty name is not an identity, so this is null too rather than a name two annotations could share.

cases.name: the-last-annotation
cases.covers: Deleting the final entry, which shifts nothing. The envelope still reports a refetch, because the page had weak annotations and an old snapshot can hold an index from before they were strengthened.
